title: Exact evidence indexing for computationally efficient structured probing
question: Can an exact inverted evidence index retain the activation-trace information advantage while reducing candidate-side probe-selection work at large M?
hypothesis: Indexing candidate-predicted structured evidence will materially improve total information gained per accounted computational work at M=512 while producing exactly the same selected probe and information score as exhaustive scanning.

arms.name: trace_exhaustive
arms.intervention: G-CASM-015 activation-trace selector scans all M candidates for every legal input-row action

arms.name: trace_indexed
arms.intervention: exact inverted evidence index uses candidate-signature bitmaps to evaluate each action without scanning all candidates

endpoints.name: total_information_per_work_m512
endpoints.role: primary — seed-level paired difference in activation-trace information gain per explicit amortized total work at M=512

endpoints.name: selector_exact_action_agreement
endpoints.role: secondary — fraction of paired trials where indexed and exhaustive selectors choose the identical row

endpoints.name: information_score_agreement
endpoints.role: secondary — numerical agreement of indexed and exhaustive information gain and expected residual candidate count

endpoints.name: expected_remaining_candidates
endpoints.role: secondary — residual hypothesis ambiguity after the selected one-step trace probe

endpoints.name: selector_work_units
endpoints.role: secondary — explicit candidate-side selector work for exhaustive versus indexed evaluation

endpoints.name: amortized_total_work_units
endpoints.role: secondary — cache plus index-build amortization plus selector and environment work

exactness_requirements: indexed selector must reproduce exhaustive selected action exactly
indexed information gain must equal exhaustive information gain within floating tolerance
indexed expected remaining candidate count must equal exhaustive value within floating tolerance
target evidence is never used before action selection

cost_model.cache_work: same G-CASM-015 trace candidate-cache work and charged once per seed
cost_model.cache_amortization: divide per-seed cache work by 160 registered tasks
cost_model.indexed_index_build: 512 * 16 posting writes; prediction cost is zero because the exact activation traces are already in the shared G-CASM-015 cache
cost_model.indexed_selector: for each of 16 actions, number of indexed signature buckets times ceil(M/64) bitmap-word units; all 16 action scans are charged
cost_model.environment: same expected trace acquisition cost as G-CASM-015
cost_model.full_total: cache amortization + index build amortization + selector work + environment work

primary_endpoint.seed_aggregation: mean across 32 tasks per seed, then paired indexed_minus_exhaustive difference across five seeds

leakage_rules: the index is built only from public candidate-predicted evidence
the target identity and target index never enter the index query or selector
the realized target trace is exposed only after the row action is selected
no result from 017 is used to tune the index structure or M
the exact activation-trace semantics are unchanged

decision_rule.condition: indexed selector is exactly action-equivalent and primary total-cost interval is positive at M=512
decision_rule.licenses: evidence that exact evidence indexing makes structured probing more computationally efficient on the registered finite workload.
decision_rule.does_not_license: learned autonomous probing or asymptotic complexity.

decision_rule.condition: indexed selector is exact but total-cost interval is not positive
decision_rule.licenses: candidate-side indexing does not recover a total-cost advantage at M=512 under this accounting.

decision_rule.condition: indexed selector is not exactly equivalent to exhaustive
decision_rule.licenses: infrastructure failure; no scientific efficiency claim is made until repaired or a new experiment is preregistered.

schedule.note: Exact indexed selector comparison; no parameter learning.
